A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Manchu in-context translation study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the relocation of v1 Appendix D to v2 Appendix I.

before.justification: v1 reports original component ablations, comparisons across LLMs, character-substitution experiments, and mT5 data-augmentation results in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds expert human assessments, Manchu-to-Chinese results, vocabulary analysis, and a grammar-order control.

M1.justification: The morphological analyzer, dictionary retrieval, BM25 examples, grammar and CoT components, character-substitution procedure, and mT5 augmentation method remain unchanged. The Chinese experiment applies the existing pipeline; replacing 'encryption' with 'encipherment' is terminology editing.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds Manchu-to-Chinese evaluation using GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3. v1 already used Manchu-Chinese material to construct English data but did not evaluate Chinese outputs. This extends target-language coverage while retaining the original Manchu-English coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained experiments is unchanged: the same Llama3 sizes, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and prompting controls remain. The new human and Chinese evaluations reuse existing models or variants rather than introduce additional comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 introduces a substantial new evaluation protocol: three bilingual experts score adequacy from 0 to 100 for three GPT-4o variants on 33 randomly selected sentences, producing 99 anonymized, randomly ordered items. Appendix F also introduces Jieba segmentation for Chinese evaluation. Existing automatic-evaluation and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a targeted control testing grammar without retrieved parallel examples, addressing possible masking of grammar benefits. Appendix E adds a vocabulary-overlap diagnostic, finding 25% unmatched English test subwords versus 3% for Manchu. Existing component ablations, model-size analyses, and output examples are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates without these statistical assessments. v2 adds 1,000-sample bootstrap significance tests for component comparisons in Appendix G, plus human-score normalization, inter-rater Pearson correlation, and Wilcoxon rank-sum tests in Section 5.3. These introduce substantive statistical support without establishing any increase in model-training runs.

E6.justification: Original Tables 1–6, Figures 2–3, and matched appendix examples retain their results. Substantial new outcomes include human adequacy scores of 29.04, 56.12, and 64.47 for direct, enciphered, and original prompting respectively (Table 7), and Chinese BLEU scores of 5.21 for GPT-4o and 9.28 for DeepSeek-V3 (Table 9). Grammar-control, vocabulary-overlap, and significance findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The mathematical prompt formulation and character-substitution mapping are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added statistical procedures do not introduce new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: dictionaries and relevant parallel examples help most, grammar and CoT offer little benefit, in-context learning explains much of performance, and synthetic data can improve low-resource NMT. New evidence supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendices D–F add localized interpretations concerning masked grammar benefits, English vocabulary mismatch as a possible cause of low overlap metrics, and linguistic or metric explanations for Chinese results. Section 5.3 interprets the nonsignificant human-score difference between original and enciphered outputs. The existing generalization and CoT limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies detailed human-rating instructions and scoring examples; Appendix F identifies the Chinese resources and Jieba implementation. These improve documentation of the added evaluations. Appendix C's generation and fine-tuning hyperparameters and the code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references for transfer learning, human assessment, forward translation, and Chinese evaluation. Section 5.2 newly positions the cipher experiment relative to Yuan et al. (2024) and Marmonier et al. (2025). The overall research positioning remains stable; NLLB and BLOOM bibliographic updates do not constitute new baselines.

P1.justification: v2 contains localized copyediting, replaces encryption terminology with encipherment, retitles Section 5, and adds Section 5.3 and Appendices D–H. Output examples move from Appendix D to I. The existing narrative and main section order are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds four tables covering human scores, vocabulary overlap, Chinese translation, and significance tests, plus boxed rater instructions. Existing figures and example-table designs are retained, with caption edits, renumbering, and page reflow rather than a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v1 relied on automatic scores and illustrative examples; v2 adds blinded expert adequacy assessment, component-level bootstrap tests, and a control addressing whether parallel examples mask grammar benefits. Together these substantially strengthen validation of the central empirical claims. The human sample remains small at 33 sentences, and the Chinese test set is not clearly specified, limiting broader conclusions, but the gains in support for the main study are substantial.
